speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to begin my assessment, how long has your baby been having trouble breathing, and were there any complications during the delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the history of 32 weeks gestation and maternal gestational diabetes raises concern for respiratory distress syndrome or transient tachypnea. Did the baby require immediate resuscitation or assistance with breathing at birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity (32 weeks gestation).
